goal: Guide AI agents to generate portable uidl-runtime UIDL JSON for other projects.

inputShape.intent: What visual artifact to generate: website, dashboard, document, slide deck, spreadsheet, or mixed app shell.
inputShape.audience: Who will use or read the artifact.
inputShape.brand: Tone, color, density, typography, and visual references.
inputShape.data: Rows, metrics, chart data, document facts, slide points, or spreadsheet values.
inputShape.session: Optional user, roles, and boolean permissions provided by the host application.
inputShape.routeModel: Optional route paths that host apps will handle through onRouteChange.

outputRules: Return one valid UIDLDocument JSON object.
Use existing widget types before inventing custom widgets.
Put reusable shells, cards, page headers, document sections, slides, and sheet layouts under definitions.
Instantiate reusable templates with componentId and slots.
Use dataSources for tables/charts instead of embedding large repeated UI manually.
For live API data, use an api action with dataSource pointing to a state path, then bind widget rows from state.api.*.rows.
Never assume API calls are enabled by default; host projects must pass apiAllowlist for trusted hosts.
Use visibility.condition with session.permissions.* for RBAC menu/page/section visibility.
Use navigate actions for route changes and let the host app handle actual routing.
Keep authorization enforcement in the host/API; UIDL visibility is UI gating only.
minimumValidation: renderUIDocument(document, { dataSources: document.dataSources, session }) does not throw.
API-backed documents render after mocked fetch responses populate the configured state paths.
Important text labels render in a DOM smoke test.
If RBAC is used, denied navigation/page sections are absent for a restricted session.

apiDataPattern.hostRequirement: Pass apiAllowlist: ['mock.uidl-runtime.local'] or an equivalent predicate.
